newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SBC Warburg, JP Morgan to head Swiss telecom deal.
newsitem.headline: SBC Warburg, JP Morgan to head Swiss telecom deal.

text.p: The Swiss government said it had named SBC Warburg and J.P. Morgan to act as global coordinators for a planned partial privatisation of the state-owned Swiss telecommunications authority Telecom PTT.
The decision was made jointly by the Federal Finance Ministry and the Federal Transporation and Energy Ministry, which also oversees the PTT, the government said in a statement.
"The two banks should work closely with the Federal Government and the Telecom PTT in order to make possible a flotation of Telecom in the second half of 1998," the statement said.
The governemnt said a definite decision on the flotation would be made by the Federal Cabinet after adoption of a new telecommunications law.
The law calls for transforming the Telecom PTT into a public company with special status as of January 1, 1998.
The move will thus allow sale of Telecom PTT, which is to be renamed Swisscom as of October 1, 1997.
The sale of Telecom shares is to be done worldwide over through an as-yet unnamed banking syndicate, the government said.
